_metadata.purpose: Why each brain region carries the band it carries, graded against an external standard. Replaces a hardcoded "not reviewed by an expert" string applied to all 38 regions regardless of evidence.
_metadata.reference: Terminologia Neuroanatomica (TNA), FIPAT 2017 — the official IFAA/FIPAT neuroanatomical terminology. IFAA Executive validated 2016-09-22; FIPAT accepted 2016-09-24; IFAA General Assembly approved London 2019. TNA terms are in the public domain.
_metadata.reference_companion: ten Donkelaar HJ, et al. Towards a Terminologia Neuroanatomica. Clin Anat. 2017;30(2):145-155.
_metadata.verification: Entry numbers and section placement read directly from the published TNA chapter-1 (central nervous system) text, extracted from the official PDF and re-verified this session. The site was unreachable from one agent environment; the extraction is cached locally, so these claims are reproducible without network access.
_metadata.not_verified: Kandel 6th ed., which source_bibliography names as the basis for these assignments, was NOT consulted. No claim here rests on it.

tiers.tna_concordant: The band equals the structural division TNA assigns. A textbook fact, not an inference.
tiers.declared_functional_grouping: The band is a circuit-function grouping that departs from TNA topography. Legitimate, but a declared choice: the page must say so and name the TNA division.
tiers.contradicted: The band is inconsistent with the structure and should be changed.

_metadata.name_collision_warning: TNA holds TWO similar terms that are different structures: 2532 "Nucleus basalis" = basal nucleus of Meynert (the Ch4 cholinergic source), and 2506 "Nucleus basalis lateralis" = basolateral amygdaloid nucleus. Confusing them is the most likely origin of the shipped error in which basal_forebrain_cholinergic listed its origin as basolateral_amygdala. Any future work naming a "basal nucleus" must state which.
_metadata.caveat: This grades region-to-band assignment only. It says nothing about whether any TARA technique implicates any region, and licenses no claim about cognitive content.

wernicke.note: Eponym, not a TNA term. The division is certain; the referent is disputed (Binder 2015).

stn.note: Banded N5 by basal-ganglia circuit function. TNA places it in the subthalamus, i.e. diencephalon.

substantia_nigra.note: Banded N5 by basal-ganglia circuit function. TNA places it in the midbrain.

vta.note: Banded N5 by mesolimbic circuit function. TNA places it in the midbrain; synonym "ventral tegmental area of Tsai".

cea.note: Banded N5 as centromedial, striatal-like amygdala; TNA records "Archistriatum" as a synonym.

bla.note: Banded N6 as the pallial, cortex-like amygdala, opposite CeA. NOTE the collision below.

hippocampus.note: Banded N6. TNA classes it as archicortex, not isocortex, so it is correctly NOT N7.

insula.note: Banded N6. Cortical, and within the TNA limbic lobe.

acc.note: Banded N6. Cortical, and within the TNA limbic lobe.

cingulate.note: Banded N6. Cortical, and within the TNA limbic lobe.

cauda_equina.note: Banded N1 Spinal Cord, which is wrong. The cauda equina is the bundle of lumbar, sacral and coccygeal nerve ROOTS distal to the conus medullaris. VERIFIED: "Cauda equina" occurs 0 times in the published TNA central-nervous-system chapter. Rescoped in place on the region (scope_review, branch fix/lane1-data-defects); N1 is retained only as a legacy address and is not a claim of cord membership.
